newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to foster permanent job contracts - Labour Min.
newsitem.headline: Spain to foster permanent job contracts - Labour Min.

text.p: The Spanish government will help firms which favour permanent contracts over temporary ones, Labour Minister Javier Arenas said on Tuesday.

"(...) traditionally in Spain we had many fiscal incentives, subsidies and few aids in terms of social security (payments). It seems to me that it is the government who has to make a clear effort to transform temporary contracts into permanent," Arenas said in a radio interview.
On Monday unions and employers signed a labour reform deal, aimed to ease a rigid labour market and curb the highest jobless rate in Europe.
"To have more stable jobs, the government has to make its own bet....we intend to lend support for social security (payments) to firms, or to contracts which opt for permanent jobs," he said.
But he did not spell out in precise terms what measures were planned.
Arenas also said he is expecting a favourable trend in employment, explaining that some factors, such as low interest rates, were in favour of more new jobs in the coming months.
"I think that recently growth data such as the interest rates trend, inflation, and the battle against the public budget deficit...are all factors which should favour more new jobs," he said.
Arenas also reiterated that the Spanish government hopes to have the labour deal ready for legislation by mid-May.
